title: Affinity JS Runtime Architecture, V8 Engine & Sandbox Limits
subtitle: Embedded V8 Execution, Module Resolution & Sandboxed Security

learningObjectives: Understand how Serif Affinity 3.0 embeds the Google V8 JavaScript engine directly inside its C++ process.
Import native modules using CommonJS syntax: `require('/application.js')` and `require('/document.js')`.
Understand sandbox boundaries: why direct arbitrary disk I/O throws PERMISSION_DENIED and how `Application.userDesktopPath` governs write access.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: Starting in Affinity 3.0, Serif introduced a modern programmatic automation architecture powered by an embedded Google V8 ECMAScript engine. Rather than relying on legacy OS-level AppleScript or COM interfaces, Affinity executes JavaScript directly within its high-performance C++ document memory model. Scripts execute synchronously on the main application thread or asynchronously via promises. For security, the runtime runs inside a strict MSIX application sandbox: scripts cannot execute arbitrary shell binaries or write to arbitrary system folders without explicit user permission. All core automation interfaces are exposed via native virtual root modules such as `/application.js`, `/document.js`, `/shapes.js`, and `/layereffects.js`.

technicalEvidence.source: Affinity 3.3.3 Embedded Google V8 Runtime & Application Module API Reference

stepByStepInstructions.title: Import the Native Application Module
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Open the Affinity Academy MCP Playground or scripting runner. At the top of your script, import the Application class using the mandatory slash-prefixed path: `const { Application } = require('/application.js');`.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Log Runtime Information to the Console
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Output the application version and product details using `console.log()`: `console.log('Product:', Application.productFullName); console.log('Version:', Application.version);`.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Inspect the Sandboxed Desktop Path
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Query the user's desktop boundary path: `console.log('Desktop Boundary:', Application.userDesktopPath);`. Notice this path points to the authorized user workspace.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Execute Script and Capture Output
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Click 'Run Script' (or execute via the `execute_script` tool). Observe the execution time (~85-100ms) and the exact string returned in the execution console.

visualExamples.title: Sandbox Security Constraints
visualExamples.description: What scripts can and cannot access.
visualExamples.visualContent:
| Capability | Allowed / Restricted | Behavioral Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Query App & Doc DOM | ALLOWED | Instant synchronous access to document scene graph |
| Create Shapes & FX | ALLOWED | Parametric vector generation via Shape classes |
| Render Spreads | ALLOWED | Generates JPEG/PNG snapshots via MCP render engine |
| Arbitrary Disk Write | RESTRICTED | Sandboxed; writing outside user folders throws PERMISSION_DENIED |
| Launch OS Binaries | FORBIDDEN | Cannot spawn external CLI processes (prevents exploits) |

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Omitting the leading slash in require statements
commonPitfalls.solution: Affinity's virtual module resolver requires a leading forward slash (e.g. `require('/application.js')`). Omitting it throws 'Module not found'.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Attempting to use ES module import syntax inside execute_script
commonPitfalls.solution: The Affinity 3.0 embedded V8 scripting sandbox evaluates standard CommonJS `require()`. Use `const { ... } = require('/module.js')`.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Writing files to arbitrary C:\ folders and getting PERMISSION_DENIED
commonPitfalls.cause: Affinity runs as a sandboxed WindowsApp (MSIX); saving to root folders like `C:\` or `C:\Windows` is strictly blocked.
commonPitfalls.solution: Save files only within `Application.userDesktopPath` or user-granted document directories.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the correct syntax for importing the Application class in an Affinity JavaScript DOM script?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Affinity's embedded V8 runtime uses CommonJS syntax with root-level virtual module paths starting with a forward slash: require('/application.js').

knowledgeCheck.question: Why does attempting to write a file to 'C:\Windows\temp' throw a PERMISSION_DENIED error in an Affinity script?
options: Because JavaScript does not have file write capabilities.
Because Affinity runs inside a hardened application sandbox that restricts filesystem access to authorized user folders such as Application.userDesktopPath.
Because your Affinity license has expired.
Because the hard drive is full.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Affinity 3.0 implements strict sandbox boundaries to prevent untrusted scripts from modifying system files or executing unauthorized code on the host machine.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does `Application.documents.current` return when no document is open in Affinity?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: When zero documents are loaded in the application workspace, Application.documents.current evaluates to null. Scripts should always verify `if (doc) { ... }` before accessing properties.

summaryPoints: Affinity 3.0 embeds Google V8 for native, high-performance DOM automation.
Native modules are loaded via CommonJS syntax with leading slashes (`/application.js`, `/document.js`).
Application sandbox security prevents destructive host OS modifications while exposing full graphic control.
The DOM API executes with sub-100ms latency directly inside the running process.

slides.title: Affinity JS Runtime & Architecture
slides.subtitle: Programmatic Design Automation with Embedded Google V8
slides.contentMarkdown:
Welcome to **Affinity Scripting & MCP Automation**.

Design is no longer limited to manual mouse dragging. In modern creative workflows, **programmatic automation** handles generative art, automated data merges, batch resizing, and visual quality assurance.

In this lesson, you will master the **internal Google V8 runtime, native module resolution, and security boundaries** of Affinity 3.0.

actionBox.label: Architectural Truth
actionBox.text: Affinity executes JavaScript directly inside its C++ memory model—not through slow browser bridges.

slides.title: The Embedded V8 Engine
slides.subtitle: Sub-Millisecond Synchronous Execution
slides.contentMarkdown:
How does Affinity 3.0 execute your code?

- **Embedded Google V8:** The same ultra-fast engine powering Node.js and Google Chrome.
- **Direct C++ Binding:** When you call `doc.addNode()`, V8 directly manipulates the internal C++ scene graph with zero IPC latency.
- **Sandbox Isolation:** Scripts run inside a secure container. Arbitrary OS command execution is prohibited, preventing security exploits.

visual.content: JavaScript Code ---> [Embedded Google V8] ---> [C++ Scene Graph] ---> [Instant Canvas Render]

slides.title: The Root Module Ecosystem
slides.subtitle: CommonJS Virtual Paths
slides.contentMarkdown:
Affinity exposes its DOM through clean virtual modules:

- **`/application.js`:** `Application.version`, `Application.documents`, `alert()`, `confirm()`.
- **`/document.js`:** `Document.current`, `sessionUuid`, `spreads`, `addNode()`, `saveAs()`.
- **`/shapes.js`:** `ShapeRectangle`, `ShapeEllipse`, `ShapePolygon`, `ShapeStar`.
- **`/layereffects.js`:** `GaussianBlurLayerEffect`, `OuterShadowLayerEffect`.

**Syntax Rule:** Always include the leading forward slash in `require('/module.js')`!

actionBox.label: Syntax Alert
actionBox.text: require('/application.js') is VALID. require('application.js') will FAIL.

slides.title: Runtime Pitfalls & Security Sandbox Limits
slides.subtitle: Avoid Syntax and Permission Errors
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Missing Leading Slash in Require
- **Error:** `Module not found: application.js`
- **Fix:** Always write `require('/application.js')` with a leading slash.

### 2. ES Module 'import' Syntax
- **The Issue:** Writing `import { Application } from ...` throws a syntax error.
- **Fix:** Affinity V8 uses CommonJS `const { ... } = require(...)`.

### 3. File System PERMISSION_DENIED
- **The Issue:** Attempting to write to `C:\test.afphoto` fails.
- **The Fix:** The MSIX sandbox allows writing only to authorized user paths like `Application.userDesktopPath`.

actionBox.label: Golden Rule
actionBox.text: Always write scripts using CommonJS require() with leading slashes.
